question: A teacher's project instructions have grown to several pages, and she notices less room for the lesson material she pastes into chats. What is the best adjustment?
options: A) Duplicate the instructions into project knowledge as well, so that Claude encounters them twice over.
B) Leave the instructions exactly as they are, since project instructions never take up any conversation space.
C) Trim the instructions to the essentials, since they occupy window space in every chat inside the project.
D) Move the instructions into the first message of every chat so they no longer take up any window space.
correct_answers: C) Trim the instructions to the essentials, since they occupy window space in every chat inside the project.
explanations: Incorrect. Duplicating them consumes more space rather than less, and repetition does not make guidance more reliable.
Incorrect. They do take up space in every chat in the project, which is precisely why she is seeing less room.
Correct. Project instructions are carried into each conversation in the project, so keeping them concise leaves more of the window for the material she is actually working on.
Incorrect. The same words consume the same space wherever they sit, and she also loses the durability of project instructions.
